Wedding.title: A R150,000 wedding costs you R1.2 million: the maths
Wedding.desc:
R150,000 on the wedding day. Gone by midnight.

The same R150,000 invested at 7% a year for 30 years: about R1,217,475. Eight times what you put in.

It's your day. Spend it your way. Just know the price.
Illustration only: assumes a steady 7% yearly return, compounded monthly, before fees, tax and inflation. Real returns vary. Not financial advice.
#wedding #investing #southafrica #personalfinance #shorts

CarFinance.title: A R400,000 car costs R574,341: the vehicle finance maths
CarFinance.desc:
R400,000 financed over 72 months at 12.75% (prime 10.75% + 2): R7,977 a month.

Total paid: R574,341. Interest alone: R174,341.

A car loses value. The interest doesn't. Do the maths before you sign.
Illustration: no deposit, fees or balloon payment. Your rate will differ. Not financial advice.

MillionRetire.title: A million rand sounds like a lot. In retirement it's R3,333 a month
MillionRetire.desc:
A common rule of thumb: draw 4% of your savings a year. 4% of R1 million is R40,000 a year, about R3,333 a month.

Want R20,000 a month? That's R240,000 a year. You'd need R6 million saved.

So the number isn't a million. Find your own, and start early.
Illustration: the 4% rule is a rule of thumb, not a guarantee. Before tax and inflation. Not financial advice.
#retirement #southafrica #savings #personalfinance #shorts

Mattress.title: Cash in a drawer loses over half its value in 20 years
Mattress.desc:
R100,000 in a drawer. The number never changes. But prices rise 4% a year.

After 20 years, it buys what R45,639 buys today. R54,361 lost, and you never spent a cent.

Money has to move to keep its value.
Illustration: steady 4% yearly inflation, no interest earned. Real inflation varies. Not financial advice.
#inflation #savings #southafrica #personalfinance #shorts
